lockCaptureWindowMs.source: authored: DW-166 -- no artifact names this figure. Measured 2026-09-05 at this tree by driving the Lock lane on-axis from (170, 440, 13.5) (the sw_lock_lane / sw_lock_1..3 corridor's own centreline, x = (150+190)/2): at ~800 mm/s (a capturing shot) s_lock_lane closes at tick 378 and the first bd_lock slot (s_lock_1) closes at tick 512 -- a 134-tick capture latency. At the measured non-capturing band's own ~575 mm/s (epic-2-context.md: "measured threshold 550-600 mm/s"), s_lock_lane closes at tick 415 and s_lock_1 does not close until tick 696 -- a 281-tick gap, the ball having rattled back down the corridor and only settling into the slot much later than any real capture would read as resolved. 180 ms sits 46 ticks (34%) above the fast, genuine capture (134 ticks) and 101 ticks (56% of the gap) below the slow shot's own late, non-credited settle (281 ticks) -- inside that gap, DW-166's discriminating condition (this story's Design Notes) correctly reads the fast shot as captured and the slow one as an unresolved closure, emitting nothing for it, exactly as AC 6 requires.

popKickMmPerS.source: authored: no planning artifact states a pop-bumper kick strength. [CORRECTED, Story 2.3, DW-160: the three claims this string previously made -- a ~180 mm/s floor, a ~220 mm/s ceiling from Top-lane cross-pop bouncing, and 126.8 mm of trailing progress at 200 as the representative escape -- were re-swept directly against the DW-148 column ((130, 850), test/pop-bumper.test.ts's own dw148TrailingProgressMm(v)) and only the last one reproduces.] There is NO floor beyond "nonzero": every positive kick tried down to 0.5 mm/s clears the strand (progress ~309 mm); only 0 mm/s (no kick) reproduces the original permanent rest. The landscape above that is NOT a clean one-sided window -- it is chaotic (this is a ball descending onto a near-symmetric octagon apex, POP_KICK_TIE_BREAK_MM only resolves the exact on-axis tie): a fine sweep at 1 mm/s resolution through 155-221 mm/s finds narrow re-strand dips interleaved with clearing bands (e.g. 164-169, 175, 178, 185-195, 197-198 mm/s each re-strand at a NEW equilibrium near (93, 840) -- just outside sw_pop_1's own north edge -- while 196, 199-202 and 205-220 clear, some robustly (~309 mm, e.g. 215-220) and some marginally (~50-130 mm, e.g. 200's own 126.8 mm)); a clean re-strand band then holds from 221 mm/s (measured 1.3 mm progress) through at least 230, with one anomalous escape at 245 before re-stranding again by 260. The ORIGINAL ceiling reasoning (Top-lane cross-pop-bouncing tick-budget exhaustion) is real but starts far higher (~425-600 mm/s per lane) than previously claimed and is not what bounds the safe range from above -- the 221 mm/s re-strand is. 200 sits inside a locally-clearing pocket (199-202 all clear) but its nearest re-strand neighbour is only 2 mm/s away at 198, not the 21 mm/s the far (221 mm/s) cliff alone would suggest -- the true margin is narrower than a single-sided reading implies, a property of the chaos itself rather than of this particular value: no nearby integer value sits in a wider uniformly-clearing pocket without moving toward the robust-but-still-cliff-bounded 215-220 band, which trades a marginal-but-real escape for a razor-thin (1 mm/s) upper margin instead. 200 is kept: it reproduces the same 126.8 mm escape this constant has always shipped with, that escape is measured, not merely inferred from the far cliff, and Story 2.3's own re-record already carries this correction.

bonusCountMs.source: authored: PRD FR-20 states the count-up mechanism ("categories count up, then the multiplier is applied") but no pace for it. bonusLetterValue.source: authored: PRD FR-20 names DRAGON letters as a bonus category but states no per-letter value. bonusLoopValue.source: authored: PRD FR-20 names the Loops as a bonus category but states no per-loop value. notes:
stateHash() hashes the whole game tree, which includes machine.deviceSlots -- this golden therefore freezes the LOOP-WRITTEN value of deviceSlots (sim/loop/index.ts:341-344, the live AD-7 violation tracked as DW-70) as part of its reference hash. If Story 2.5's fix is faithful the values will be identical and nothing breaks; if this golden ever breaks on deviceSlots alone, check DW-70 before assuming the physics changed. Story 2.1b (2026-09-01): header.tableHash/assetHash refreshed against the completed shot-map registry and collision document (TABLE gains ~31 switches, 7 coils and bd_lock; the collision document gains ~27 col_ nodes), header.gameStart.tuning unchanged (no TUNING value moved). expectedHash/expectedGameStateHash moved: bd_lock adds a slots entry to every snapshot's machine.deviceSlots, changing GameState's own shape regardless of trajectory -- booted [true, true, true] under the then-unconditional fill(true) default, corrected to [false, false, false] by Story 2.1d (see that story's own note below); 'empty-slots' was never accurate for this pass. Rework iteration 2 (2026-09-01), correcting this note: the sentence that used to stand here -- blaming "Blender's alphabetical bpy.data.objects ordering" reshuffling existing nodes' own array positions, with an "order-sensitive broadphase" -- was investigated and found FALSE, twice: the collision document is alphabetically sorted throughout, so the ~28 new names interleave among the existing ones rather than reshuffling their relative order, and a document rebuilt with the rework's own wall-height and deflector changes reverted reproduces the two affected goldens bit-identically, ruling out node reordering as the mechanism. The TRUE cause of the two affected goldens' own trajectory divergence was not identified by either the implement pass or this rework; DW-53's wall-height change (col_wall_left/_top/_right/_lane now reaching the glass) and DW-58's col_lane_deflector removal were both tested and ruled out individually (each reproduces the divergence bit-identically when reverted alone). State plainly rather than guess further: the trajectory changed because the shot map's own regeneration changed the collision document in some way this investigation did not isolate -- not because of the specific mechanism previously claimed here. This golden's own recorded scenario was re-verified against the refreshed run and still holds at the recorded transitions/coilPrologue/durationTicks (byte-identical, untouched). Rework iteration 3 (2026-09-02): header.assetHash refreshed again (the deflector re-site / col_loop_top shorten / sw_drain widen, DW-121) -- this golden's own 800-tick window never leaves the shooter lane, nowhere near any of this pass's changes; expectedHash and expectedGameStateHash are UNCHANGED, confirmed by a fresh run. Story 2.1c (2026-09-03), the ORBIT: header.assetHash refreshed ONLY. Both recorded hashes are byte-identical before and after the geometry change, as expected -- this golden never leaves the shooter lane, so none of the re-drawn shot map is on its path.
